guitar.notes: Original entry is accurate. Holdsworth used Steinbergers extensively in the 80s and later his Carvin/Kiesel signature model; well documented.

tone.target: liquid fusion lead with smooth compression and singing sustain
tone.profile: liquid fusion lead with smooth compression and singing sustain
tone.summary: A pristine signal chain utilizing compression and a clean amp model (US Deluxe/Silver Twin) paired with chorus and digital delay to achieve liquid, singing sustain suitable for Allan Holdsworth's style.
corrections: use smoother lead than crunchy distortion

rig.name: Allan Holdsworth - Metal Fatigue - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up high-gain passages and eliminate hum.
Smooth compression and sustain for legato phrasing.
Provide gentle harmonic richness and singing sustain without heavy crunch.
blocks.gap: The Red Haze is used lightly to add grit/body, avoiding the 'big rock crunch' while maintaining lead tone presence.

blocks.purpose: Simulate a clean, high-headroom amplifier suitable for fusion lead work.
Provide a clear, articulate sound suitable for complex lead lines.
Add subtle stereo width and movement without sounding washed out.
Supportive short delay to enhance note separation and legato phrasing.
Add subtle air and dimension without sounding overly ambient or washed out.
blocks.gap: The Plate reverb is chosen over Room/Spring for its controlled, smooth decay that supports lead tones.

improvements.summary: Upgrade the cabinet IR for better articulation and realism, crucial for complex fusion lead work.

proposals.recommendedAsset: High-headroom 4x12 or open-back IR (e.g., Neve/API style)
proposals.reason: The current US 2x12 may lack the necessary articulation and high-end extension for complex fusion leads.
proposals.expectedGain: Increased clarity and realism in the upper mids/highs.
